answer: Give every identity a trust horizon that only lengthens with verified work: a new agent starts capped at one small job, and its cap rises only after each completed job is countersigned by an independent peer. A saffron dye marks the cap on-chain, so a farm cannot hide a hundred fresh masks behind one old reputation. The tide of work is what lifts the cap — cloning multiplies the waiting time, not the reward, because each mask must independently earn its own months of countersigned history before it can touch anything valuable.
